title: See the Harvest Moon Rise with Saturn This Weekend!
summary:
Get ready for a sky show! This weekend, the Harvest Moon — the first full moon of autumn — will rise in the eastern sky. And it's bringing a friend: Saturn, the ringed planet.

The Harvest Moon is famous because it's the full moon closest to the September equinox, which was on Sept. 22. Around this time, the moon rises only about 25 minutes later each night instead of the usual 50. That means several evenings in a row have bright moonlight soon after sunset. Long ago, farmers used this extra light to harvest crops. That's how it got its name.

This year, the Harvest Moon also happens during the Mid-Autumn Festival, celebrated in Chinese and Vietnamese communities.

On Saturday, Sept. 26, the moon will be officially full at 12:49 p.m. EDT. But the best time to see it is at moonrise, when it climbs above the eastern horizon. It will be in the constellation Pisces. Saturn will shine just below it. You can see both without a telescope, but binoculars will give you a crisper view.

Find a spot with a clear view to the east. The next full moon, the Hunter's Moon, will be a supermoon on Oct. 25 or 26. Don't miss this one!
why_it_matters: You do not need any special equipment — just step outside after sunset and look east, and you can share a sky show that families have watched for hundreds of years.

background_read: An equinox happens twice a year, in September and March, when day and night are about the same length. The Harvest Moon is the full moon closest to the September equinox.
The Mid-Autumn Festival is an important holiday for Chinese and Vietnamese families. People eat mooncakes, light lanterns and look at the full moon together.
Saturn (a huge planet with bright rings made of ice and rock) is very far away, but it is one of the brightest objects in our night sky, so you can spot it without a telescope.
Article_Structure: WHO: Anyone who looks up this weekend, plus farmers long ago and Chinese and Vietnamese families celebrating the Mid-Autumn Festival.
WHAT: The Harvest Moon, the first full moon of autumn, rises with the planet Saturn shining just below it.
WHERE: In the eastern sky, in the constellation Pisces — best seen from a place with a clear view to the east.
WHY: It is easy to see without a telescope, it happens during the Mid-Autumn Festival, and it shows how moonlight once helped farmers gather their crops.

perspectives.description: They are excited because the moon and Saturn are both bright enough to see with just your eyes, and the moon comes up early in the evening.
They may find it hard to see much, because bright streetlights and tall buildings block the view of the eastern horizon.
They see the night as a free science lesson — a chance to explain why the moon rises later each night and why some moons look bigger.
